mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport P400 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Range Rover Sport P400 engine typically costs between £4,500 and £7,000 for supply only. Reconditioned units start around £3,500, while used engines can be found from £2,500. Prices vary based on whether you choose supply-only or a full supply and fit service.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of ignition or injector failure in a Range Rover Sport P400?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include a rough idle, hesitation under acceleration, and an illuminated check engine light (often with misfire codes P0300-P0306). You might also notice reduced fuel economy or a slight loss of power due to direct injector coking.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport P400?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the current premium vehicle market. A well-maintained Range Rover Sport P400 holds a value of £25,000 to £75,000+. Investing £4,500-£7,000 in a rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is financially viable and protects the appreciating asset value of this premium SUV.

mainEntity.name: What is the AJ300 engine code in the Range Rover Sport P400?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AJ300 is the specific 3.0-litre inline-six Ingenium petrol engine code fitted to the Range Rover Sport P400 (producing 400PS). It features advanced direct injection, a twin-scroll turbocharger, and a 48V mild-hybrid electrical system (MHEV) for improved efficiency and torque fill.

mainEntity.name: How does the 48V mild-hybrid system affect a Range Rover Sport P400 engine replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AJ300 engine in the Range Rover Sport P400 is integrated with a 48V Belt-integrated Starter Generator (BiSG). Replacing the engine requires specialist high-voltage safety protocols and precise software recalibration to ensure the combustion engine and MHEV system communicate correctly with the ECU.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Sport P400 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport P400 utilises the modern 3.0-litre Ingenium inline-six petrol (AJ300), which offers strong performance and mild-hybrid efficiency but has documented vulnerabilities. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Ignition Coil & Injector Coking - Why the Range Rover Sport P400 AJ300 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Direct injection leads to carbon buildup on intake valves and injector tips. Combined with the high thermal load of the twin-scroll turbo and electric supercharger, this accelerates ignition coil degradation, causing misfires, rough idling, and check engine lights (codes P0300-P0306).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Ignition coil replacement, walnut blasting for carbon removal, and software updates
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage misfires without internal mechanical damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, revised injectors, upgraded coils, and 48V system diagnostic check, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution for persistent misfires, severe coking, or concurrent 48V integration faults

Given the premium valuation of the P400, a rebuilt or reconditioned engine is a financially sound investment that protects the vehicle's strong retained asset value.
problems.recommendation: If your Range Rover Sport P400 is exhibiting early signs of misfiring or rough idling, a targeted preventative repair (coil replacement and carbon cleaning) is highly cost-effective. However, if the engine has suffered from prolonged neglect, severe injector coking, or concurrent 48V system faults, a full rebuilt unit is the only reliable long-term solution to protect your investment.
